question: Should OpenClaw permanently support denylist entries in both tools.exec configuration and exec-approvals.json that force one-shot human approval over security=full, ask=off, allowlists, and durable trust?
rationale: Technical review supports the implementation shape, but cannot decide whether two persisted authorization surfaces and changed full/off semantics should become a permanent product security contract.

options.title: Accept both after proof
options.body: Retain both denylist layers and their one-shot human-only precedence after exact-head live hot-revocation proof is supplied.

options.title: Limit to approvals file
options.body: Remove tools.exec.denylist and keep the STOP list solely in the host-owned approvals policy.

options.title: Decline deny-over-allow
options.body: Close the feature if full/off must remain uninterruptible and operators should use allowlist mode instead.

recommendation.title: Accept both after proof
recommendation.body: Retain both denylist layers and their one-shot human-only precedence after exact-head live hot-revocation proof is supplied.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work owns the authorization transaction and delayed-policy semantics changed by this contract.
